summary.text: 南 is attested for “south” in Shang oracle-bone inscriptions. The object shown in its early graph is disputed, and the surviving proposals do not establish how the graph’s original use relates to the direction word.

formation.text: The graph’s formation is disputed. Proposed readings include a hanging percussion instrument, a house front, and a covered vessel with a plant-like form above. The vessel reading supports a proposal that the graph first wrote 醓, “meat sauce.” The received Shuowen analysis treats 𣎵 as semantic and 𢆉 as phonetic, but the phonetic role lacks a suitable historical sound comparison in the evidence here.

history.text: The graph is recorded in oracle-bone, bronze, manuscript, and seal forms. The ancient form 𡴖 is also recorded, but the available accounts do not show a continuous sequence from the Shang forms to the later character.

Shang inscriptions use 南 for the direction, in the ancestor name 南庚, and for a sacrificial item. The proposed account that an instrument sign was reused for “south” would require the object-name and direction word to have sounded alike or similar; the object’s identity and ancient name and pronunciation remain unsettled, and the inscriptions do not establish which use came first.

uncertainties.text: The early graph’s referent is disputed among instrument, house-front, covered-vessel, and other proposals. A proposed lexical link between “south” and a belly or front-of-body word concerns the spoken word’s history; it does not establish the graph’s formation or a semantic path.
The exact earliest inscription and the order of the reported Shang uses are unresolved; a continuous graphic derivation is also not established.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone inscriptions; exact earliest specimen date unresolved
senses.text: 南 is attested for the direction “south” in Shang oracle-bone inscriptions. This establishes an early use, not that “south” was the graph’s original meaning.
南 is also used for a southern part; its date relative to the directional sense is unresolved here.
南 is also used to mean southward; its date relative to the directional sense is unresolved here.

limitations.text: The reported ancestor-name and sacrificial-item uses do not establish separate character senses or a chronology among the Shang uses.
The evidence does not establish a transition among the Shang uses or sound-based borrowing from an instrument name to write “south.”
The proposed lexical link between “south” and a belly or front-of-body word does not establish a semantic development.

overview.text: 南 means “south” and is attested for that direction in Shang inscriptions. Its early graph’s referent is disputed. A proposed borrowing from an instrument-name would mean the sign was reused because the words sounded alike or similar, but the name and sound are unsettled.

limitations.text: No verifiable glyph image is available to illustrate 南’s early form or its graphic history. The proposed oracle-style redraw has no usable image link, and no alternate image was established with both verified identity and accessible image data.
